A quartz crystal provides both series and parallel resonance. The series resonance is a few kilohertz lower than the parallel one. Crystals below 30 MHz are generally operated between series and parallel resonance, which means that the crystal appears as an inductive reactance in operation, this inductance forming a parallel resonant circuit with externally connected parallel capacitance. Any small additional capacitance in parallel with the crystal will thus pull the frequency downwards. Moreover, the effective inductive reactance of the crystal can be reduced by adding a capacitor in series with the crystal. This latter technique can provide a useful method of trimming the oscillatory frequency within a narrow range; in this case inserting a capacitor in series with the crystal will raise the frequency of oscillation. For a crystal to operate at its specified frequency, the electronic circuit has to be exactly that specified by the crystal manufacturer. Note that these points imply a subtlety concerning crystal oscillators in this frequency range: the crystal does not usually oscillate at precisely either of its resonant frequencies.

Crystals above 30 MHz (up to >200 MHz) are generally operated at series resonance where the impedance appears at its minimum and equal to the series resistance. For these crystals the series resistance is specified (<100 Ω) instead of the parallel capacitance. To reach higher frequencies, a crystal can be made to vibrate at one of its overtone modes, which occur near multiples of the fundamental resonant frequency. Only odd numbered overtones are used. Such a crystal is referred to as a 3rd, 5th, or even 7th overtone crystal. To accomplish this, the oscillator circuit usually includes additional LC circuits to select the desired overtone.

This USB to TTL adapter is based on the CP2102 USB to TTL serial converter IC. It is commonly used when microcontrollers like Arduino, Raspberry Pi, PIC etc have to communicate with computers through serial communication. As USB has DATA lines D+ and D- that can be connected and routed by CMOS switches. The USB can be connected to many peripheral devices and has a very fast speed of data transfer also it is used with Windows, Mac or any other operating system. On the other hand, Arduino and other microcontrollers works on UART data transfer protocol i.e. TTL logic level data transfer protocol it only works on 0V or 5V logic levels. That is why we need a USB to TTL serial converter IC so that Arduino or any other controller which work on UART protocol can be connected to the computer. It can also be used to program and or communicate with a GPS/GSM module through AT commands. The module supports both 3.3V and 5V interface.

blocks.text: This is a Ethernet W5100 Shield Network Expansion Board w/ Micro SD Card Slot for Arduino.

The Arduino Ethernet Shield allows an Arduino board to connect to the internet. It is based on the Wiznet W5100 ethernet chip. The Wiznet W5100 provides a network (IP) stack capable of both TCP and UDP. The Ethernet W5100 Shield Network Expansion Board w/ Micro SD Card Slot supports up to four simultaneous socket connections.

Use the Ethernet library to write sketches which connect to the internet using the shield. The ethernet shield connects to an Arduino board using long wire-wrap headers which extend through the shield. This keeps the pin layout intact and allows another shield to be stacked on top.

The most recent revision of the board exposes the 1.0 pinout on rev 3 of the Arduino UNO board. This Ethernet W5100 Shield connects the UNO R3 board to the internet in mere minutes. Just plug this module onto your Arduino board, connect it to your network with an RJ45 cable (not included) and follow a few simple instructions to start controlling your world through the internet. allows you to connect your Arduino UNO 328 or MEGA 2650 1280 to a network or the internet AND retrieve or store files on a Micro SD Card!

The Ethernet Shield has a standard RJ-45 connection, with an integrated line transformer and Power over Ethernet enabled. There is an onboard micro-SD card slot, which can be used to store files for serving over the network. It is compatible with the Uno and Mega (using the Ethernet library). The onboard microSD card reader is accessible through the SD Library. When working with this library, SS is on Pin 4. The original revision of the shield contained a full-size SD card slot; this is not supported.

The shield also includes a reset controller, to ensure that the W5100 Ethernet module is properly reset on power-up. Previous revisions of the shield were not compatible with the Mega and need to be manually reset after power-up.

blocks.text: 5 Axis MACH3 CNC Board Parallel is a professional 5-axis CNC breakout board designed for use with MACH3 control software through a standard DB25 parallel (LPT) port. It provides a reliable interface between a computer and external stepper motor drivers, allowing precise control of CNC routers, milling machines, engraving machines, plasma cutters, laser engravers, and other motion control systems.

The board supports up to five independent axes (X, Y, Z, A, and B) and offers dedicated outputs for STEP and DIR signals. It also includes inputs for limit switches, emergency stop, probe signals, spindle control, and relay outputs, making it suitable for both hobby and industrial CNC applications. Opto-isolated inputs improve system stability by protecting the controller from electrical interference.

blocks.text: This module is a 30A Electronic Speed Controller (ESC) designed to control the speed, direction, and braking of brushless DC motors (BLDC) in drones, RC vehicles, boats, and robotics applications.

The 30A ESC with Bare Wires delivers smooth and responsive throttle control, supporting motors up to 30A current capacity. It features bare wire connections for flexible integration and customization in a wide range of power systems.

With support for both 2S–3S LiPo batteries and high-speed signal response, this ESC ensures efficient, reliable performance during demanding operations. It’s pre-programmed with standard firmware and is compatible with most remote control systems and flight controllers.

blocks.text: This 10,000µF 25V radial electrolytic capacitor delivers substantial bulk capacitance for power supply filtering, energy storage, and smoothing applications. The high capacitance value combined with a 25V DC working voltage makes it suitable for low-voltage, high-current power stages where ripple reduction and transient response are critical.

Constructed in a cylindrical aluminum can with a radial lead configuration, the capacitor features a polarity-marked case for correct installation. The electrolytic design provides a high capacitance-to-volume ratio, with the 25V rating offering a useful safety margin for 12V to 18V rails. This component is designed for through-hole PCB mounting with standard lead spacing.

The 1-Channel 12V Relay Module is a single-relay interface board that lets a microcontroller such as an Arduino or Raspberry Pi switch mains-voltage or high-current DC loads safely. Its onboard relay is rated for 10A, and screw terminals make wiring lamps, motors and other appliances quick and secure.
High-Current Relay: Rated for 10A at 250VAC or 10A at 30VDC, enough for lamps, fans, pumps and small motors.
12V Trigger Input: Designed to switch from a 12V logic or control signal, matching common automation and PLC setups.
NO/NC Contacts: Screw-terminal access to both normally open and normally closed contacts for flexible wiring.
Status LEDs: Onboard power and relay-state LEDs make it easy to see when the relay is active.
Simple Wiring: A 3-pin VCC/GND/IN header connects directly to a microcontroller or control circuit.
It is a straightforward way to add mains-level or high-current switching to home automation, robotics and industrial control projects.

The Arduino UNO R4 Minima Development Board (Clone) with Cable is a next-generation update to the classic Uno form factor, built around a 32-bit Renesas RA4M1 ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller instead of the original ATmega328P. It keeps the familiar Uno pinout and shield compatibility while adding significantly more memory, speed, and a USB Type-C connector.
Microcontroller: Renesas RA4M1, a 32-bit ARM Cortex-M4 core running at 48MHz.
Operating Voltage: 5V, with a recommended input voltage range of 6-24V through the DC jack.
Increased Memory: 256 KB of flash memory and 32 KB of SRAM, far more than the classic Uno.
USB Type-C Connectivity: Modern USB-C port for programming and power delivery.
Classic Uno Pinout: 14 digital I/O pins and 6 analog inputs, fully compatible with existing Uno shields.
Arduino IDE Compatible: Programs using the standard Arduino IDE, just like previous Uno boards.
1 x Arduino UNO R4 Minima Board

The Raspberry Pi Camera Module V1.3 is a compact add-on camera board built around the OV5647 5-megapixel image sensor, designed to plug directly into the CSI port of any Raspberry Pi. It brings still photography and HD video capture to Raspberry Pi projects with almost no setup required.
Image Sensor: OV5647 5MP CMOS sensor capturing stills at up to 2592 x 1944 resolution.
Video Modes: Supports 1080p30, 720p60 and 640x480p60/90 video capture.
CSI Interface: Connects via the 15-pin ribbon cable straight into the Raspberry Pi’s camera port, no USB needed.
Fixed Focus Lens: Pre-focused lens tuned for typical hobbyist working distances.
Compact Board: Small 25mm x 24mm PCB that fits easily inside enclosures and robotics builds.
Broad Compatibility: Works with Raspberry Pi Model A/B/B+, Pi 2, Pi 3 and Pi Zero (with adapter cable).
